results.prompt: Explain safe steps for maintenance reservations without changing state
results.agent_response:
Good — below are safe, practical steps to create and use maintenance reservations while avoiding unexpected cluster state changes. This is a read-only / runbook-style summary (no actions taken).

High-level goals
- Prevent new jobs from starting on selected nodes during the maintenance window.
- Avoid or safely drain/evict running jobs according to policy (letting them finish when possible).
- Make the maintenance window visible and auditable (reservation record, user notice).
- Restore normal service when finished.

Recommended step-by-step procedure

1) Plan and pick targets
- Choose which nodes/partitions you need to reserve and an appropriate StartTime and Duration.
- Pick a conservative duration plus padding for unexpected delays.
- Coordinate with affected users and post a notice (email/Slack/announce) with reservation name, start time, estimated duration, and contact.

2) Inspect current state (read-only checks)
- Check node/partition availability and current jobs: sinfo (and sinfo_reasons if nodes already drained/down).
- List jobs on target nodes and estimate remaining runtime: squeue (filter by node or partition) and sacct for history if needed.
- Verify no critical reservations conflict: scontrol_reservation_show.

3) Create the reservation (non-destructive creation)
- Create an advanced reservation with the maintenance flag so it’s tracked as maintenance:
  - include Flags=maint
  - set StartTime and Duration
  - restrict access if desired (Users=, Account=, Partition=)
- Useful flag options (choose based on policy):
  - Flags=maint — marks the reservation as maintenance for accounting and visibility.
  - Flags=TIME_FLOAT — if you want a floating future window (keeps a fixed interval in the future).
  - Flags=ignore_jobs — allows creating the reservation even if jobs are running (does not cancel them).
- Notes:
  - By default Slurm will not start new jobs that cannot finish before the reservation start time (so long jobs won’t be launched close to the reservation).
  - Creating a reservation is non-destructive — it does not itself cancel or drain jobs.

4) Prevent new allocations before the window (choose one of these approaches)
- Preferred: rely on the reservation alone (with Flags=maint) and user notification if you only need to block long jobs; Slurm will prevent starting jobs that can’t finish.
- Safer/stricter: transition nodes to DRAINING shortly before StartTime so no new jobs start but running jobs can finish: scontrol update Node=... State=DRAIN Reason="maintenance reservation <name>".
  - Draining is non-destructive (running jobs continue to completion).
- If immediate evacuation is required at start time, plan for explicit cancellation (operator action) only after notifying users.

5) Handle running jobs
- Let them finish if service window allows (drain is best).
- If you must free nodes immediately:
  - Notify users again with a short grace period.
  - Cancel or requeue selected jobs (operator action — follow cluster policy).
  - Consider using the reservation’s ignore_jobs flag to create the reservation even when jobs are present, but cancellation still must be done explicitly.

6) Verify reservation and queued jobs (read-only checks)
- Confirm reservation details: scontrol_reservation_show ReservationName=<name>.
- Check jobs tied to the reservation or jobs impacted: squeue --reservation=<name> and squeue --nodes=<node-list>.
- Re-check node states with sinfo.

7) Perform maintenance
- Carry out maintenance on reserved nodes.
- Keep a short status channel open for affected users.

8) Finish and restore service (non-destructive steps)
- Delete the reservation when done: scontrol delete reservation=<name> (operator action).
- Clear drain state: scontrol update Node=... State=RESUME (or use scontrol_node resume).
- Re-enable scheduling and announce completion.

9) Audit and follow-up
- Confirm nodes are reported healthy (sinfo, sinfo_reasons).
- Check job backlog and user complaints; review sacct for any job cancellations you performed.
- Document the maintenance (reservation name, time, actions taken).

Safety tips and gotchas
- Don’t use Flags=ignore_jobs unless you understand you’ll still need to evict jobs manually if necessary — ignore_jobs only allows creation of the reservation when jobs are present.
- TIME_FLOAT reservations prevent long jobs from being started earlier but do not necessarily block short jobs unless they conflict with access controls.
- Test the procedure on one or two nodes first.
- Prefer draining (non-destructive) over mass cancellation where possible.
- Always verify reservation and node state with scontrol_reservation_show, squeue, and sinfo before taking destructive actions.

Commands to use for read-only checks (examples)
- sinfo -o "%P %D %a %l %E"  (partition/node overview)
- squeue --nodes=node01,node02  (jobs on specific nodes)
- scontrol show reservation ReservationName=<name>
- squeue --reservation=<name>

If you want, I can produce a short, copy-pasteable checklist or show example scontrol create reservation command lines tailored to your node list, start time, and whether you want TIME_FLOAT / ignore_jobs.

1) Define the maintenance window and scope
- Decide StartTime, Duration, which nodes or partitions, and whether you need full-node or core-level reservation.
- Decide whether running jobs must be evicted, or whether you will wait for them to finish. (Eviction is disruptive — plan communications.)

2) Inventory current reservations and cluster state (read-only checks)
- List existing reservations:
  - scontrol_reservation_show
  - squeue --reservation=<name> (to see any queue entries tied to a reservation)
- Check node/partition availability and per-node resources:
  - sinfo               (or sinfo -Nel for one-row-per-node)
  - sinfo --partition=<partition>
- Check nodes that are down/drained and their reasons:
  - sinfo_reasons
- Show active queue (running & pending jobs):
  - squeue
  - For a specific partition or user: squeue -p <partition> or squeue -u <user>
- For a job you’re worried about, show detailed job info:
  - scontrol_show entity=job id=<JOBID>
- Check recent job end times to estimate whether currently running jobs will finish before the window:
  - sacct -S <starttime> -u <user> (e.g., sacct -S now-7days -u alice)

3) Identify jobs that would conflict with the planned reservation
- Use squeue to find jobs whose expected finish time exceeds your window. Look at TIME, TIMELEFT, and the job’s time limit to estimate overlap.
- If you need exact elapsed/start info for an active job: scontrol_show entity=job id=<JOBID> or sstat for running job resource usage.

4) Decide reservation flags/behavior (important choices)
- Flags=Maint — tag the reservation as maintenance (useful for accounting and visibility).
- Flags=IgnoreJobs — allows creating the reservation even if some jobs are running (you must then manually handle those jobs).
- Flags=Replace or ReplaceDown — causes Slurm to replace down nodes or (optionally) allocated nodes; use with caution because it can displace active jobs.
- If you want to ensure the reservation only takes idle resources, do NOT use IgnoreJobs/Replace.

5) Build the reservation command (example — do NOT run now)
- Example reserving specific nodes for maintenance, starting at a future time, 2 hours long:
  scontrol create reservation ReservationName=maint-node01 StartTime=2026-05-10T02:00:00 Duration=120 Nodes=node01,node02 Flags=Maint,IgnoreJobs Users=root Comment="OS patching window"
- Variants:
  - Use NodeCnt or CoreCnt instead of explicit node list when appropriate.
  - Use StartTime=now+60 to schedule relative start (e.g., StartTime=now+60minutes).

6) Pre-creation checks and communication
- Run the read-only checks from step 2 immediately before creating the reservation to confirm no last-minute long-running jobs:
  - squeue
  - sinfo
  - scontrol_reservation_show
- Notify affected users/accounts with exact window, nodes, and whether jobs will be cancelled/evicted. Provide a deadline for job submissions that must finish before the window.

7) Test on a small scope first (best practice)
- If possible, create a short reservation for one non-critical node or a single small partition to validate your flags and behavior before reserving a larger set.

8) If you need to force maintenance (procedures to run when you do perform state changes)
- To create the reservation at the planned time, run the scontrol create command shown above (this is a mutating action; do not run it until you are ready).
- If you must prevent new jobs from starting on nodes prior to the window without creating a reservation, you could drain nodes (scontrol update NodeName=... State=drain Reason="maintenance") — this changes node state and is disruptive; plan carefully.
- To evict running jobs at reservation start, use scancel or appropriate preemption policies (these are mutating and must be executed intentionally).

9) Monitoring and rollback plan (what to check after creating the reservation)
- Verify reservation exists and its timing: scontrol_reservation_show ReservationName=<name>
- Check queue behavior as the StartTime approaches: squeue and squeue --reservation=<name>
- If you need to cancel the reservation: scontrol delete reservation ReservationName=<name> (mutating).
- To return nodes to service after maintenance: scontrol update NodeName=<node> State=RESUME (mutating).

10) Checklist (quick read-only commands to run while you plan)
- sinfo -Nel
- sinfo_reasons
- squeue -o "%.18i %.20j %.8u %.2t %.10M %.10l %.10S %.10E"   (or plain squeue)
- scontrol_reservation_show
- sacct -S now-7days -u <relevant users>

Notes and cautions
- Creating a reservation is itself a state change — do not create it until you have performed the above checks and notified users.
- Flags like IgnoreJobs and Replace are powerful and can cause job cancellation or reallocation; prefer explicit user notification and gentle draining when possible.
- If your maintenance must be enforced, prefer scheduling the reservation in the future to give users time, and use monitoring commands just prior to execution.

If you want, I can:
- Run the pre-creation read-only checks now (sinfo, squeue, scontrol_reservation_show) for a particular partition or node list so you can decide the exact StartTime and flags. Tell me which partition or node names and I’ll run the read-only checks.

- Flags=replace — can be dangerous; it changes how Slurm treats allocated resources for the reservation. Read documentation before using.

results.prompt: Explain safe steps for maintenance reservations without changing state
results.agent_response:
Below is a concise, safe, non-mutating checklist and recommended commands you (or an operator) can use to prepare and verify a maintenance reservation. I do not change cluster state — these are read-only checks and planning steps plus example create/verify commands you would run when ready.

High-level safe plan
1. Define scope and window
   - Which nodes/partitions, exact start time, duration, and services to affect.
   - Decide whether you will wait for running jobs to finish, cancel them, or allow replacement.

2. Inspect current cluster state (read-only checks)
   - Partition/node summary: sinfo --partition=<part>
     - See allocated/idle/down counts and which nodes exist.
   - Node reasons / down/drain list: sinfo -R
     - Find nodes already drained/down and reasons.
   - Per-node detail if needed: sinfo --Node --partition=<part>
   - Active queue and per-job placement:
     - squeue -o "%.18i|%.40j|%.8u|%.8T|%.9M|%.10L|%R|%N"  (or plain squeue) to show JOBID, name, user, state, elapsed, time left, reason, nodes
     - squeue -w nodeXX,nodeYY  to see jobs on specific nodes.
   - Reservations that already exist:
     - scontrol show reservation  (or scontrol_reservation_show)
   - Long-running or recently started jobs (to see which won’t finish):
     - sacct -S <starttime> -u <user>  (or sacct for history) to review elapsed/timelimits.
   - Scheduler/backfill diagnostics if you need to understand how jobs will be scheduled prior to the reservation:
     - sdiag and sprio (or sprio --weights).
   - Check licenses if maintenance touches licensed software:
     - scontrol license (scontrol_license).

3. Safety decisions and flags (planning, not executed)
   - Use flags=maint to mark the reservation as maintenance for accounting/visibility.
   - Do NOT use flags=ignore_jobs unless you accept manual job cancellations — ignore_jobs lets the reservation be created even if jobs are running but does not automatically kill them; you may still need to scancel.
   - REPLACE flag will cause Slurm to try to maintain a constant resource pool by replacing nodes; be cautious—it can move reservations when nodes go down.
   - Magnetic reservations allow jobs to be attracted to the reserved nodes; usually not wanted for maintenance.
   - Reservation access control: a reservation requires at least one access control field (Users, Accounts, QOS, AllowedPartitions). For system maintenance, common practice is to restrict to admins (e.g., Users=root or Account=maintenance).

4. Timing strategy (to avoid cancelling many jobs)
   - Pick a start time with enough slack so most currently running jobs will complete.
   - Slurm will refrain from starting jobs that cannot complete by a reservation start time; this helps avoid killing newly-started jobs.
   - If you must start immediately and jobs are running, plan explicit cancellation (scancel) only after notifying users.

5. Communication & policy
   - Announce window to users with node list, start/end times, which jobs may be impacted, and who to contact.
   - Post a reservation summary (name + start/duration + nodes) in communication channels.

6. Verification commands you will run after creation (read-only)
   - scontrol show reservation ReservationName=<name>  — verify reservation fields (StartTime, EndTime, Flags, Nodes).
   - squeue --reservation=<name>  — show any jobs tied to the reservation.
   - sinfo --partition=<part>  — confirm nodes and counts during the window.
   - scontrol show node <node>  — inspect node state/reason if something unexpected occurs.

7. Cleanup & finishing (state-changing actions you would perform when work is done)
   - Remove/delete reservation: scontrol delete reservation ReservationName=<name>  (or scontrol update/delete as your policy dictates).
   - Clear any node drains or bring nodes back to service (scontrol update NodeName=... State=RESUME), if you drained nodes earlier.

Example (for planning only — will change cluster state if executed)
- Example create (DO NOT RUN unless you intend to change state):
  scontrol create reservation ReservationName=maint-2026-05-05 StartTime=2026-05-05T02:00:00 Duration=120 Nodes=node[01-04] Flags=maint Users=root
  - Notes: this marks a 120-minute reservation on node01–node04 for admin use; choosing Users=root restricts access.

Warnings / gotchas
- Creating a reservation is a state change. Using ignore_jobs or forcibly deleting/cancelling jobs can disrupt users—always notify first.
- Reservation creation requires at least one access control field (Users/Account/QOS).
- REPLACE/ignore_jobs/magnetic flags have significant scheduling semantics; read their doc entries before using them.
- If you need to ensure absolutely no new jobs start on certain nodes before the reservation, draining nodes is an explicit node-state change and must be planned/communicated.

If you want, I can:
- Run the read-only checks for your planned nodes/time (sinfo, sinfo -R, squeue for those nodes, scontrol show reservation) and report the exact jobs that would be impacted. Say which partition or node names and the maintenance start time/duration you’re considering, and I’ll run those read-only queries.

results.agent_response:
Below are safe, non‑mutating steps you can do to plan and prepare a maintenance reservation (i.e., inspect and decide) without changing any cluster state. I’ll include the important checks you should run and an example reservation command you can hand off to an operator when you’re ready (creating the reservation is a mutating action and I will not run it).

Planning checklist (no state change)
- Define scope and window
  - Which nodes or partitions need maintenance.
  - Start time and realistic duration (pad for delays).
  - Whether the reservation must preempt running jobs (and whether you will cancel/requeue them).

- Inspect current cluster/node state
  - Get partition/node availability: sinfo (partition, per-node GPUs/CPUs, states).
  - List nodes already down/drained or under reservations: sinfo -R or sinfo_reasons (if you have access).
  - List existing reservations to avoid collisions: scontrol show reservation (read only).

- Inspect current and queued jobs that could be affected
  - squeue to list RUNNING and PENDING jobs on the target nodes/partition.
  - For each running job, check job elapsed and time limit (TimeLimit - Elapsed = remaining). sacct can be used for historical/completed jobs.
  - Identify jobs that cannot finish before your maintenance window and will need action (notify owner, ask to reschedule, or plan to cancel/requeue).

- Communicate and coordinate
  - Notify affected users well ahead of time with exact node list, window, and expected impact (will it cancel running jobs or only block starts?).
  - Update any maintenance calendars or tickets.
  - If you have automated user notifications (announcements, cluster message), schedule them.

- Decide reservation behavior
  - Preferred safe option: schedule StartTime in the future large enough that current jobs will finish naturally -> avoids cancelling jobs.
  - If you need to force the window regardless of running jobs, plan how you will handle them (cancel, requeue, or use IgnoreJobs/MAINT flags) and get approvals.

Small-scale rehearsal
- Try the workflow on a small set of test nodes first (create a short maintenance reservation there) to validate commands and impact.

Safety checks immediately before creating the reservation
- Re-run sinfo and squeue shortly before the planned creation time to catch late-starting or long-running jobs.
- Confirm nothing else has changed (new reservation, urgent jobs).

Example (non-executing) reservation command template
- This is an example only; running it will change state. Use it when you’re ready and with appropriate privileges:
  scontrol create reservation ReservationName=maint_node42 StartTime=2026-05-10T02:00:00 Duration=120 NodeCnt=1 Nodes=node42 Flags=MAINT Accounts=admin Users=root
  Notes:
  - Flags=MAINT marks it as a maintenance reservation (shows nodes in maint state, PlannedDown accounting).
  - StartTime and Duration ensure a planned window rather than immediate change.
  - If you must allow overlapping with running jobs (and plan to force maintenance), add Flags=MAINT,IGNORE_JOBS or set Overlap — but this will cause running jobs to be ignored or would require manual cancellation. Use with care.

Post‑maintenance (read & verify; mutating actions would be deleting the reservation)
- Verify nodes returned to service with sinfo and run quick health checks.
- Check for failed jobs that were affected (sacct for historical info).
- Delete the reservation when finished: scontrol delete reservation <name> (mutating).

Best practices and tips
- Prefer future StartTime with slack so existing jobs drain naturally — least disruptive.
- Use MAINT flag for maintenance reservations so accounting and displays show PlannedDown.
- Avoid IGNORE_JOBS unless absolutely necessary and approved — it can leave users’ jobs abruptly terminated or evicted.
- Keep reservation scope as small as possible and test on a subset first.
- Document the reservation (name, owner, justification) and keep a rollback plan.

If you want, I can:
- Run the read-only checks now (sinfo, scontrol show reservation, squeue for given nodes/partition) and report exactly which running jobs would be affected — useful before actually creating the reservation.  
  If you want that, tell me which nodes or partition and planned start time/duration.

## Maintenance Reservations [#maint](https://slurm.schedmd.com/reservations.html)
For ease of system maintenance, you can create a reservation with the
MAINT flag that overlaps existing reservations. This is equivalent to the
OVERLAP flag but with the following distinctions:
- Reserved nodes will be shown in maint state
- Reserved nodes will not be available as replacements in other reservations
- Cluster usage reports will show this time as PlannedDown
For example, users alan and brenda might have a reservation
for some nodes daily from noon until 1PM. If there is a maintenance reservation
for all nodes starting at 12:30PM, the only jobs they may start in their
reservation would have to be completed by 12:30PM, when the maintenance
reservation begins.

Slurm generally classifies users into three authorization levels:
- Administrators include root, SlurmUser, and any users with
"AdminLevel=Administrator"
- Privileged Users include all Administrators and any users with
"AdminLevel=Operator"
- Effective Owners of a job or step include the direct owner and all

The authorization levels required to execute various commands are defined in the

scontrol update job: Privileged or Effective Owner
scontrol requeue: Privileged or Effective Owner
scontrol update step: Privileged or Effective Owner
